description: Bitcoin Address Behavior Dataset -- 544,462 labeled Bitcoin addresses across 13 behavior classes, 148 features.
citation: Yuchi Xiang et al. 2024. BABD: A Bitcoin Address Behavior Dataset for Pattern Analysis. IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security.
code_repo: https://github.com/Y-Xiang-hub/Bitcoin-Address-Behavior-Analysis (Apache-2.0 -- covers the collection/preprocessing code, NOT a statement about the dataset's own redistribution terms)
license_note: Kaggle's dataset page states no explicit license (page is JS-rendered, not readable via unauthenticated fetch -- same limitation already documented for other Kaggle sources in docs/CRYPTO_DATASET.md). Treat as non-redistributable, same policy as external_data/ellipticpp: kept local, gitignored, never republished.
dataset_version: as downloaded from Kaggle by the project owner, 2026-09-07
acquisition_note: Downloaded manually by the project owner via a Kaggle account (this environment has no Kaggle API credentials) and supplied at ~/Downloads/BABD-13.csv; copied into place, not fetched by any script here.

schema_notes.columns: account (real base58 BTC address), SW (SA=Strong Address / WA=Weak Address -- the paper's own label-confidence distinction), 148 numeric behavioral feature columns, label (0-12).
schema_notes.label_map_source: Cross-checked against arXiv 2204.05746 Table I's per-class address counts -- every one of the 13 counts in the paper matched this CSV's own label-value counts exactly (0:8686, 1:91617, 2:13861, 3:300000, 4:180, 5:9309, 6:105257, 7:27, 8:16, 9:15, 10:1580, 11:12412, 12:1502), confirming the index order independently rather than assuming it.

data_quality_findings.exact_duplicate_rows: ~527 rows are byte-identical repeats of another row (same account, same SW, same label) -- deduplicated on ingestion, same policy as external_data/ellipticpp.
data_quality_findings.label_conflicts: 1,414 accounts (0.26%) appear more than once with DIFFERENT label values across their rows (3,216 rows total) -- a real upstream data-quality defect, not a parsing error (verified by direct inspection, e.g. account 149w62rY42aZBox8fGcmqNsXUzSStKeq8C is labeled both class 0 (BLACKMAIL) and class 8 (MONEY_LAUNDERING) in different rows). These are never resolved by picking one label arbitrarily -- see tools/build_crypto_benchmark.py's load_babd13_wallets, which marks them ground_truth_label=LABEL_CONFLICT and excludes them from any label-based split or the balanced subset.
